reason: The PROBLEM is real and I verified it in the source and by driving the page; the FIX is wrong, so this is refuted per the rule that a correct problem with a wrong fix is refuted with the corrected fix supplied. On the problem: lately.html movementThree() renders LIMITS as three .limit tiles and then a sibling .ghost carrying only class="ghost rise" and style="--i:2" - no id, no role, no aria-labelledby, no data attribute. Driven at 1440 the three tiles are 351px wide at x=206/573/939 and .ghost is 1084px at x=206, so it spans all three equally and no visual tie exists either. The seat understates the ambiguity: the caption's noun 'recorder' lexically matches tile TWO ('The date recorder switched on in August'), while its concept - three periods of earlier readings to compare - matches tile ONE ('the snapshot writer has no callers yet, so there are no earlier readings to compare'). The copy therefore pulls toward two different tiles at once, and the twelve bare columns name no metric and no axis, so the drawing does not disambiguate. In the one movement whose whole value is that the limit is stated where the reader would assume the opposite, an unattributed illustration that reads as covering all three refusals - two of which have unrelated causes and one of which is a Notes change, not this product's - is a genuine loss. This is not restating a gate: interaction-check.mjs lines 390-407 assert only that the band exists, that it has three tiles, that the ghost has >=8 columns and >80px height, and that its heading ranks with movement one. Nothing there asserts any binding between plot and tile. It is also in scope - polishing a protected object, not shrinking, removing or redesigning it, and it adds no colour and no weight. WHY THE FIX IS WRONG: the a11y half is inert. .ghost is a bare <div>, so its implicit role is generic, and ARIA prohibits name-from-author on generic - browsers and screen readers will not expose an accessible name, so id + aria-labelledby buys literally nothing while looking like it did. It is also unnecessary: .ghost-plot is already aria-hidden="true" and .ghost-say is real DOM text in reading order immediately after the third tile, so fixing the visible heading fixes the spoken version for free. The fix's mechanics are also wrong against the real source: LIMITS is rendered through .map(([head, why]) => ...) with a hardcoded style="--i:1" on every tile, so there is no 'first .limit heading' to hang an id on without threading the map index through - the fix as written cannot be applied as described. Severity is correctly classed: the ghost under-attributes, it does not assert something untrue, so defect - not misleading, not blocking - is right.
sharpenedFix: Do the tie in visible copy and native semantics; drop the ARIA entirely. (1) Change the ghost's own heading to name its tile: 'Open work over time - the chart we would draw', sub-line unchanged. That is what actually removes the guess, for sighted and screen-reader readers alike. (2) Make the markup say what it is: render .ghost as <figure class="ghost"> with <figcaption class="ghost-say">. figure maps to role figure, which does support a name, and figcaption gives the caption its native relationship to the drawing - no aria-labelledby, no ids threaded through the LIMITS map. (3) If a machine-readable tie is still wanted for the gate, stamp data-limit="open-work-over-time" on the figure and the matching tile rather than inventing an ARIA relationship the role cannot carry. (4) Leave the other two refusals undrawn; one plot answers one refusal, and inventing two more ghosts would turn the movement into a gallery.
breaks: The heading grows from 29 to 44 characters against .ghost-say .t-head { max-width: 26ch }, so it wraps to two lines inside a .ghost-say that is position:absolute; inset:0 over a 120px .ghost-plot - re-measure that the two-line head plus the small line still centres without colliding with the column tops, and re-check it at 390 where .limits collapses to one column (line 439) and the ghost narrows further. Converting the div to <figure> inherits the UA margin of 1em 40px, which will break the band's gap rhythm and the .ghost margin-top: var(--gap-line) - reset margin: 0 explicitly or the whole movement shifts. After it lands re-run audit.mjs (type ramp, leading, and AA contrast of the heading over the 0.5-opacity columns now that it occupies two lines and more of the plot area) and interaction-check.mjs (lines 405-407: ghostColumns >= 8, ghostHeight > 80 and the heading-rank equality are all unaffected by copy, but the .ghost-plot selector must still resolve after the figure change). Also re-check the rise stagger: --i:2 sits on the element being swapped, so confirm the entrance animation still fires on the figure.
